 - Build: `make build` (runs `scripts/build.sh`; `scripts/build.ps1` on Windows).
-- Check: `make check`.
-- Run the CLI: `make tq ARGS="<command>"`.

+  output for errors rather than trusting the exit code (or run `dotnet build Tarnquill.sln` directly).

+  `PASS`/`FAIL`; exit 0 means all passed. Add new checks as `Check(...)` calls in that project's
+  `Program.cs` — there is no xUnit/NUnit.
+- Run the CLI: `make tq ARGS="<command>"`. Run it from the repo root: `tq` uses paths relative to the
+  current directory.
+- Without `make` (e.g. Windows), use the `dotnet` commands shown in the `Makefile`.

+## The `tq` CLI
+
+- `tq env check` — verifies `git` is installed. Safe to run.
+- `tq commit` — **interactive**: prompts on stdin for a change type and a message, then runs
+  `git commit -m "<type>: <message>"`. Agents should not run it; use `git commit` directly with the
+  same format instead. Allowed types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`.

+  item overwrites the first queued one. `<id>` must be numeric.

+
+- `scripts/clean-outbox.sh` deletes every queued comment in `.tarnquill/outbox/`. It is destructive;
+  don't run it unless asked.

+  assume network access to the forge.

+exits 1 if any check failed. To add a check, add a `Check("<name>", expected, actual);` line to
+`tests/Tarnquill.Core.Checks/Program.cs`.

+Exit codes: `0` success, `1` failure, `2` usage error.

+  without input will hang or fail, so agents should not run it bare. It runs
+  `git commit -m "<type>: <message>"` on whatever is already staged, so you can follow the same
+  convention with `git commit` directly:
+  - Format: `<type>: <message>`, where `<type>` is one of `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`.
+  - Non-interactive equivalent: `printf 'fix\nhandle empty input\n' | make tq ARGS="commit"`.

+  `.tarnquill/outbox/<id>.json` (relative to the current directory; gitignored). Ids must be
+  numeric. A second comment for the same id overwrites the first. Nothing in this repo sends the
+  outbox to the forge, so don't tell the user a comment was posted.
+

+
+The forge URL comes from `TARNQUILL_FORGE_URL`. When it is unset, no forge is reachable. Don't
+make up a URL or assume network access to the forge.
+
+## Destructive scripts
+
+`scripts/clean-outbox.sh` deletes **every** queued comment in `.tarnquill/outbox/` and can't be
+undone. Ask the user before running it.

+`tests/Tarnquill.Core.Checks` is a plain console program, not xUnit/NUnit, so `dotnet test` does
+nothing useful. It prints one `PASS <name>` or `FAIL <name>: expected X, got Y` line per check and
+exits 1 if any check failed. `scripts/run-checks.sh` wraps it for CI. To add a check, add a `Check("<name>", expected, actual);` line to
+`tests/Tarnquill.Core.Checks/Program.cs`.
+
+## The `tq` CLI
+
+Exit codes: `0` success, `1` failure, `2` usage error.
+
+- `tq env check`: verifies that `git` is installed. This is the only tool it checks.
+- `tq commit` is **interactive**: it prompts on stdin for a change type, then a message. Running it
+  without input will hang or fail, so agents should not run it bare. It runs
+  `git commit -m "<type>: <message>"` on whatever is already staged, so you can follow the same
+  convention with `git commit` directly:
+  - Format: `<type>: <message>`, where `<type>` is one of `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`.
+  - Non-interactive equivalent: `printf 'fix\nhandle empty input\n' | make tq ARGS="commit"`.
+- `tq item comment <id> --body <text>` does **not** post anything. It writes the comment to
+  `.tarnquill/outbox/<id>.json` (relative to the current directory; gitignored). Ids must be
+  numeric. A second comment for the same id overwrites the first. Nothing in this repo sends the
+  outbox to the forge, so don't tell the user a comment was posted.
+
+## Forge / environment
+
+The forge URL comes from `TARNQUILL_FORGE_URL`. When it is unset, no forge is reachable. Don't
+make up a URL or assume network access to the forge.
+
+## Destructive scripts
+
+`scripts/clean-outbox.sh` deletes **every** queued comment in `.tarnquill/outbox/` and can't be
+undone. Ask the user before running it.
